title: `drawImage()` with a density-corrected `img`: image pixels or CSS pixels?

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

body:
[`drawImage()`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#drawing-images) says:

> If not specified, the *dw* and *dh* arguments must default to the values of *sw* and *sh*, interpreted such that one CSS pixel in the image is treated as one unit in the output bitmap's coordinate space. If the *sx*, *sy*, *sw*, and *sh* arguments are omitted, then they must default to 0, 0, the image's natural width in image pixels, and the image's natural height in image pixels, respectively.

For an `img` whose density isn't 1 (from `srcset` or EXIF resolution), image pixels and CSS pixels differ, and it's unclear which one the source rectangle uses or what size `drawImage(img, 0, 0)` draws at. My reading is that it draws at the density-corrected natural size (`naturalWidth`).

Browsers disagree. A 200×100 PNG drawn with `drawImage(img, 0, 0)`:

| `img` | `naturalWidth` | Chrome Canary | Firefox Nightly | Safari TP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `srcset="a.png 400w" sizes="100px"` | 50 | 50px | 200px | 200px |
| `srcset="a.png 2x"` | 100 | 200px | 200px | 200px |

[density-corrected-image-in-canvas.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/density-size-correction/density-corrected-image-in-canvas.html) seems to expect source rectangle coordinates to be density-corrected for EXIF resolution.

It'd be good to say explicitly which coordinate space the source rectangle and the default destination size use. `createImageBitmap(img)` gives a 200px-wide bitmap in Chrome Canary, Firefox Nightly, and Safari TP for both cases, so it uses image pixels; WebGL's `texImage2D()` probably needs the same answer.
